one_liner: User-mode x86-64 Linux emulator for Arm64, RISC-V and LoongArch hosts whose dynamic recompiler beats its own interpreter 5-10x.
what_it_does: Box64 runs unmodified x86-64 Linux ELF programs (games, Steam, Wine64/Proton, Java, Unity titles) on 64-bit little-endian non-x86 Linux hosts, launched as `box64 ./program` or transparently through binfmt_misc. It is a whole-program user-mode emulator, not an embeddable JIT library: guest code is translated, while calls into common system libraries (libc, libm, SDL, OpenGL, Vulkan and many more) are redirected to the host's native builds through generated wrappers. Box32 (experimental, -DBOX32=ON) adds 32-bit x86 processes and WowBox64 builds a wowbox64.dll for Wine WOW64.
how_it_is_fast: The DynaRec is a block-based dynamic binary translator: FillBlock64 in src/dynarec/dynarec_native.c runs four passes per block (pass0 finds addresses, jumps and block size; pass1 does float and flag-liveness optimisation; pass2 sizes native instructions; pass3 emits), with per-host backends in src/dynarec/{arm64,rv64,la64,ppc64le}. Speed comes from deferred and native-flag x86 EFLAGS emulation (only computing flags that are read), big blocks that run past overlaps, CALL/RET optimisation that bypasses the jump table (BOX64_DYNAREC_CALLRET=2 default), and fast-but-inexact defaults for NaN, rounding and memory ordering. Wrapping native libraries means library-heavy code (libc string routines, GL drivers) never gets emulated at all, and DynaCache (default on since v0.4.4) stores translated code under ~/.cache/box64 so second launches skip translation.
when_to_use: Running closed-source x86-64 Linux binaries or games on an Arm64 board, Snapdragon/Apple-Silicon Linux laptop, Ampere server, RISC-V or LoongArch machine where no native build exists.
Running Windows games on Arm64 Linux via Wine64/Proton (with Box86 or Wine WOW64 for 32-bit parts), where native GL/Vulkan drivers are reached through wrappers.
Workloads that spend much of their time in wrapped system libraries (libc, libm, SDL, GL), where Box64's wrapping skips emulation entirely.
Repeated launches of the same binaries, where DynaCache removes recompilation cost on the second run.
when_not_to_use: On an x86-64 host, or for 32-bit x86 programs without Box86/Box32; the DynaRec exists only for Arm64, RISC-V, LoongArch and a work-in-progress PPC64LE backend, other hosts fall back to the interpreter.
Multithreaded programs that depend on x86 total store order: BOX64_DYNAREC_STRONGMEM defaults to 0 (no barriers), so lock-free guest code can misbehave unless you raise it, which costs speed.
Code that needs bit-exact x86 floating point or exceptions: FASTNAN=1 and FASTROUND=1 are defaults, division-by-zero exceptions are off (DIV0=0) and x87 80-bit math is done in float/double.
As an embeddable JIT or library: it is a standalone executable with no API, so it is not a component you can link into your own interpreter.

Production servers that must not crash: open issues include DynaRec-only failures (Valheim server #4065, Dead Space 2 #4119, Java ZGC/G1 crashes #4023, OpenJDK 25 JIT SIGSEGV #3864) and an unsynchronised memExist() lookup reported as thread-unsafe (#3617).

integration.form: standalone executable built with CMake (registered via binfmt_misc); not a library
integration.dependencies: Python 3.7+ at build time (wrapper generation), CMake 3.19+; libz.so loaded at run time via dlopen for DynaCache compression (optional); Zydis only for trace builds; host 64-bit libraries for any wrapped library
integration.min_toolchain: C (-std=gnu11), GCC or Clang; GCC 11+ for Jetson Orin and GCC 15.2+ for the NVIDIA GB10 preset per docs/COMPILE.md
integration.platforms: Linux on 64-bit little-endian hosts: AArch64, RISC-V 64, LoongArch64 with DynaRec; PPC64LE DynaRec still WIP; x86-64 build is interpreter only (for testing); Android/Termux experimental
integration.thread_safety: Emulates multithreaded guests, but x86 memory ordering is only approximated unless BOX64_DYNAREC_STRONGMEM is raised; issue #3617 reports an unlocked memory-map lookup.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: the baseline is the same binary with BOX64_DYNAREC=0, so switching is one environment variable; against QEMU user mode it is a drop-in for x86-64 Linux programs only

gotchas: Default DynaRec settings trade accuracy for speed (STRONGMEM=0, FASTNAN=1, FASTROUND=1, DIV0=0, x87 in float/double where possible); per-program rcfile profiles in /etc/box64.box64rc override these for known-bad titles, so measured speed depends on which profile applied.
DynaCache is on by default and may use up to 2 GB in ~/.cache/box64; set BOX64_DYNACACHE=2 (read-only) or 0 to disable, and remember it when timing first versus second launches.

No benchmark harness, workload list, CPU or flags are published in the repository; the '5-10x faster than the interpreter' figure is an unqualified README claim, and the linked box86.org game-performance analysis and the EuroSys 2026 paper could not be opened here (box86.org and dl.acm.org EGRESS_BLOCKED, no PDF copy on GitHub found by two searches).

Comparisons against QEMU-TCG mix two effects: JIT quality and native-library wrapping (QEMU emulates guest libc and drivers, Box64 calls host builds), and QEMU enforces x86 ordering on weak-memory hosts while Box64 does not by default; BOX64_DYNAREC_STRONGMEM=4 exists to 'mimic x86 TSO similarly to QEMU's approach, for evaluation purposes'.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Box64 over Blink when you need to run large dynamically linked x86-64 programs or games on Arm64, RISC-V or LoongArch with native GPU drivers, since Blink is a small portable emulator measured on SSE math and short-lived processes against qemu-x86_64; pick it over research translators such as oxtra or Instrew when you need a maintained tool with Wine/Proton support rather than a paper prototype.
verified_claims_summary: The only number in the repository is the README's first-party '5-10x faster than the interpreter alone' for DynaRec builds versus Box64's own interpreter, with no workload, CPU, compiler or flags stated. The README-cited EuroSys 2026 paper (co-authored by the Box64 author) reports, per its abstract seen only in search snippets, under 40% average slowdown versus native and 3.3x over QEMU-TCG on RISC-V; its setup and benchmarks were not read.
status_note: Very active (last commit 2026-10-06, about 8,960 commits, 5.7k stars, release v0.4.4 adds DynaCache and LoongArch/RISC-V work), MIT-licensed and usable as a packaged tool via Pi-Apps-Coders debs, but the performance claim stays first-party (tier C) until the EuroSys paper's numbers are read.
